deities: Mumba Devi (form of Goddess Parvati/Amba, patron goddess of Mumbai)
Annapurna (stone figure seated on a peacock, to the left of the main shrine)

history.dynasty: None (Koli fishing-community shrine, rebuilt by merchant patrons)
history.period: Original shrine circa 1675 (some sources say 14th century); rebuilt at present site 1737 (some sources say 1766)
history.summary: Mumba Devi Temple is the shrine of Mumbai's namesake patron goddess - the city's name derives from 'Mumba' + 'Aai' (mother in Marathi). The goddess is an incarnation of Parvati, revered for centuries by the Koli fisherfolk, the city's original inhabitants, who pray to her before venturing out to sea; legend says she destroyed a demon named Mumbarka who troubled the region. Tradition holds the first shrine, Mungachi Amba, was founded by a Koli fisherwoman named Munga at Bori Bunder, near the present Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus. In the 18th century the British East India Company cleared the Esplanade for fortifications and relocated the temple to Bhuleshwar; a goldsmith, Pandurang Shivaji, financed the new construction around 1737 (some sources give 1766). In 1830 a Vania lady named Putalibai funded a tank adjoining the temple (filled in during the 1950s for parking). The black-stone idol wears a silver crown, nose stud, and golden necklace, with a tiger - the goddess's vehicle - before the sanctum. Though architecturally modest, it is one of Mumbai's most important spiritual landmarks.

name: Mumba Devi Temple
town_description: Mumbai, the capital of Maharashtra and India's financial capital, takes its name from this temple's goddess. The temple stands at Bhuleshwar in South Mumbai, amid busy markets like Zaveri Bazaar and Crawford Market, in narrow lanes of devotional shops.

travel.airport: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (~22 km).
travel.railway: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) is the nearest major railway station, close to the temple's original site; Charni Road and Marine Lines are also nearby.
travel.road: Bhuleshwar is well connected by local trains, buses, and taxis; the temple is in a crowded market area best reached on foot for the last stretch.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; avoid Monday closures.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:30 AM (Mangal Aarti) to 9:00 PM daily; closed on Mondays. Aartis: 6:30 AM Mangal Aarti, 9:30 AM Main Aarti, 12:15 PM Naivaidya Aarti, 6:30 PM Dhoop Aarti, 8:00 PM Main Aarti, 8:50 PM Shayan Aarti.
